newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher as constructions surge.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher as constructions surge.

text.p: Taiwan share prices erased early losses to finish slightly higher on Monday as the central bank's weekend decision to scrap selective credit controls on land boosted construction sector buying, brokers said.
The weighted index ended up a scant 17.57 points or 0.28 percent at 6,342.17. Turnover was T$35.46 billion.
Construction shares surged 1.18 percent. Kindom Construction rose T$1.70 or 4.24 percent to T$41.8 and Coldsun Construction was up 70 cents or 3.11 percent to T$23.2.
Sentiment was lukewarm towards Morgan Stanley's long-awaited inclusion of Taiwan into its global indices from Monday.

"The magic power of Morgan Stanley had faded," said Allen Huang of Baring Securities. "People are taking a wait-and-see attitude to watch whether foreign funds flow into the Taiwan market before they make their next move."

For weeks, investors had expected Morgan Stanley's move to boost the Taiwan market's profile and thereby attract new foreign capital. Some brokers said they had noted foreign funds entering the market to buy shares in late trade on Monday.
Brokers said the government's recent drives to boost the sluggish local economy and real estate industry would help strengthen investors' confidence.
Electronic and machinery shares were up 0.80 percent, with computer giant Acer Inc up T$1.7 or 4.76 percent to T$37.4.
Taiwan Semiconductor rose in active trade to close up 50 cents at T$55.5.
The market was expected to move narrowly on Tuesday, with initial resistance seen at the 6,400-point level, brokers said.
